lines.text: June 2026. A calf in Texas is found with maggots eating it alive.
The New World screwworm. America wiped it out in 1966. Now it's back.
A female lays up to five hundred eggs in a wound. The maggots burrow into living flesh.
And the weapon that beat it last time? More flies. Billions of them.
Sterilized with radiation, and dropped from airplanes.
Because a female mates only once. If her mate is sterile, her eggs never hatch.
Now there are seventy one cases, from Texas to Arizona.
And a new fly factory in Texas is racing to breed hundreds of millions more.
Watch the full story: how two scientists beat it with an X-ray machine.
